searchText: Howdy yall! Thank you <@!203220829473996800> for the intro 🙂 Was wondering if anyone has implemented an optimized SMT for Geth's state tree. (for context this is for off-chain state tree calculations in optimistic rollup) I think <@456226577798135808> is the right person to ask 🙂 <@!420501213327392770> Oh, no, we did not implement SMT for geth's state trie. We implemented binary version of it (but with the same patricia rules). I personally think SMT is not going far enough 🙂 Oh interesting! Is the code somewhere I can take a look at? Also, when you say SMT is not going far enough what do you mean? of course, you can look at the code, but it is quite entangled: https://github.com/ledgerwatch/turbo-geth/blob/master/trie/trie.go#L80 I mean that I would jump straight into self-balancing trees (I know there are some difficulty with the order of modifications having impact on the structure, but these could be dealt with) Awesome thank you! Didn't realize it was in master! > jump straight into self-balancing trees Ahhh yeah that makes sense. In this case self-balancing is a little more tricky because the reason I like SMTs is for their simplicity (especially when implementing it in a smart contract). But overall we definitely need some self balancing trees > Yes, for the purpose of witnesses, tries are unified. <@456226577798135808> I don't understand how this is the case. From reading the spec, it still looks to me like it "ends" in the AccountNode because it just has a `storage_root` field. <@!213672586264051717> it might be a problem with the spec then hmm, from the witness spec ``` AccountNode{nonce:Int balance:Int storage:nil|Node code:nil|CodeNode|HashNode} ``` storage is a `Node`, so it could be a `BranchNode`, `ValueNode` etc. Ah, ok, that makes sense then I thought it was just a hash <@!296630428754771968> on the call today <please-someone-fill-in-the-blank> was very interested in getting together with you on the block size and propogation time stuff. Sorry but I can't remember who spoke up, anyone able to fill in the blank? I believe it was somewhat specifically directed at understanding what our upper bounds are likely to be for overall witness sizes It was Jared Wassinger anyone know if he's on this discord? or have contact information that they could forward on to <@!296630428754771968> he used to be jwasinger#8326 in some other channel Now I'm even sadder that I missed the call, I'd love to talk to him I think getting better data on this piece could have a large impact on what the final stateless design looks like

excerpts.author: karl.tech
excerpts.content:
Howdy yall! Thank you <@!203220829473996800>  for the intro 🙂 

Was wondering if anyone has implemented an optimized SMT for Geth's state tree. (for context this is for off-chain state tree calculations in optimistic rollup)

excerpts.author: mandrigin
excerpts.content: I think <@456226577798135808> is the right person to ask 🙂

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: <@!420501213327392770> Oh, no, we did not implement SMT for geth's state trie. We implemented binary version of it (but with the same patricia rules). I personally think SMT is not going far enough 🙂

excerpts.author: karl.tech
excerpts.content: Oh interesting! Is the code somewhere I can take a look at?

excerpts.author: karl.tech
excerpts.content: Also, when you say SMT is not going far enough what do you mean?

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: of course, you can look at the code, but it is quite entangled: https://github.com/ledgerwatch/turbo-geth/blob/master/trie/trie.go#L80

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: I mean that I would jump straight into self-balancing trees (I know there are some difficulty with the order of modifications having impact on the structure, but these could be dealt with)

excerpts.author: karl.tech
excerpts.content:
Awesome thank you! Didn't realize it was in master! 

> jump straight into self-balancing trees
Ahhh yeah that makes sense. In this case self-balancing is a little more tricky because the reason I like SMTs is for their simplicity (especially when implementing it in a smart contract). But overall we definitely need some self balancing trees

excerpts.author: 0xraino
excerpts.content:
> Yes, for the purpose of witnesses, tries are unified.
<@456226577798135808> I don't understand how this is the case. From reading the spec, it still looks to me like it "ends" in the AccountNode because it just has a `storage_root` field.

excerpts.author: Deleted User
excerpts.content: <@!213672586264051717> it might be a problem with the spec then

excerpts.author: mandrigin
excerpts.content:
hmm, from the witness spec
```
AccountNode{nonce:Int balance:Int storage:nil|Node code:nil|CodeNode|HashNode}
```
storage is a `Node`, so it could be a `BranchNode`, `ValueNode` etc.

excerpts.author: 0xraino
excerpts.content: Ah, ok, that makes sense then

excerpts.author: 0xraino
excerpts.content: I thought it was just a hash
